title: Saffy and Prickles Make a Friend
markdown:
Once upon a time, Saffy the elf loved her cozy home with its soft moss cushions and windows made of amber. But her hedgehog, Prickles, often felt a little lonely by the warm fire. They lived in Whispering Snowberry. The trees there had shiny ice, like little silver bells. And the air smelled like sweet berries.

Every day Saffy fluttered about with her wings. They shimmered like dragonfly wings when the sun shone. She collected shiny dewdrop jewels, like tiny diamonds. She put them in her leaf bag and hummed a happy elf song. And Prickles? Well, Prickles trundled along. His little nose twitched with every interesting smell. He sniffed for the tastiest roots under the mossy ground. But even with Saffy nearby, it was a bit quiet for Prickles. They did not meet many friends.

Even the happiest little elf sometimes wishes for a new friend for their pet. It is a wish that tickles your heart. And that is just what Saffy was thinking one sunny morning.

Until one day Saffy made up her mind. She bounced on her tiny toes. “Prickles, you need a new friend. A very good friend. Someone to share your root-finding fun with.” So, with a determined flutter of her shimmering wings, they set off from their cozy home. Their big adventure would take them to the Glowworm Glade. It was a place of twinkling lights and soft moss, a place they had never, ever visited before.

A very good friend. That was what Prickles needed.

And as they padded along a path lined with sleepy daisies, they heard a gentle clack-clack-clack. It was a comfy sound. And there, sitting on a plump mossy log, was the biggest friendliest creature Saffy had ever seen. It was an ogre. But not a scary ogre. This ogre had a kind crinkly smile that reached all the way to his ears. His hands, as big as dinner plates, were busy knitting. He was making a very long colourful scarf that snaked across the glade like a rainbow river. His name was Grumbles, and he hummed a little tune as he worked.

“Hello.” Saffy held Prickles gently. Prickles peeked out from her hands. His little nose wiggled with curiosity at the enormous woolly creature.

Grumbles looked up, his big gentle eyes blinking kindly. “Well, hello there, little flutter-wing and spiky fellow.” His voice was like soft thunder after a summer rain. “Lovely day for a wander, isn’t it?”

“It is indeed. We are Saffy and Prickles. We have never been to the Glowworm Glade before.”

“Oh, you must see this berry.” Grumbles leaned down, his knitting still in his big hands. He wanted to show Prickles a particularly plump juicy-looking berry. But oh dear me, his knitting needle, long and smooth, accidentally nudged Prickles. With a tiny surprised eep that was barely a whisper, Prickles curled himself up into a tight spiky ball. You could not see even a little bit of Prickles’s nose.

Saffy, seeing her dear Prickles go all round and prickly, felt a little wobble in her heart, like a tiny jelly. But she remembered Grumbles’s kind smile and the gentle rumble of his voice. “It is all right, Grumbles. Prickles sometimes needs a moment to uncurl. He is just a little shy when meeting new friends.”

Grumbles’s big face fell a tiny bit. “Oh, goodness me.” He looked at his knitting needle. “I am so terribly sorry, little one. I did not mean to startle you. My hands are so big.” He felt a bit sorry, you see. He reached into his big woolly bag, rummaging around. “Here.” He pulled out a bundle of the softest fluffiest yarn Saffy had ever seen. It was the colour of moonlight. “Perhaps this might make him feel better? It is very soft. I can knit you a tiny cozy blanket for him, if you like. It will be as soft as a cloud.”

Saffy’s eyes lit up like tiny stars. “Oh, that would be wonderful.” And so, right there in the soft glow of the Glowworm Glade, a delightful scene unfolded. Saffy, with her nimble elf fingers, found a spare twig. She started knitting too. She decided to make a tiny little cap for Grumbles’s knitting needle, so it would not nudge anyone by accident again. It would be a little woolly hat, just for the needle. Grumbles, with his big gentle hands that were surprisingly careful, began to knit a small soft blanket. His needles moved with a gentle click-clack. And Prickles? He slowly, slowly began to uncurl. First a tiny nose poked out, then two bright curious eyes, and finally his whole round spiky self. He felt the soft woolly yarn beneath him, heard the gentle clack-clack of knitting needles, and smelled the sweet earthy scent of the mossy glade. He let out a contented sigh that puffed his tiny chest.

Until finally, there they were, all three of them, sitting together in perfect harmony. Grumbles, Prickles, and Saffy all sat together. Prickles, feeling quite safe and cozy on his brand-new yarn blanket, snuggled down. He was fast asleep, dreaming of yummy roots and new gentle friends. Saffy giggled, a sound like tinkling bells, and Grumbles hummed a happy rumbling tune that vibrated through the mossy ground.

Ever since then, Saffy and Prickles often visited Grumbles in the Glowworm Glade. The Whispering Snowberry felt a little less quiet. And sometimes, when the moon was high and the stars were twinkling extra brightly, you could see the soft glow of Grumbles’s knitting lamp. And if you listened very closely, past the rustling leaves and the chirping crickets, you might hear a tiny contented snore coming from a very happy hedgehog, nestled on his softest blanket. A very good friend, after all.
characters: Saffy (young elf who collects dewdrop jewels), Prickles (a hedgehog who curls into a ball)
author: StoryGen Community
